warrior.works: Strength in the legs and back, stamina and focus.
warrior.watch: Front knee past the toes, back leg soft.
warrior.easier: Shorter stance, hands on the hips.
warrior.tip: Imagine your arms pulled in opposite directions in a tug-of-war, while the torso stays exactly midway between the feet.
warrior.avoid: High blood pressure — arms not overhead; knee injury.

steps: From mountain pose step the right foot forward about a leg-length; turn the back foot out slightly, the whole sole on the floor.
Square the hips, chest and shoulders to the front.
Inhale and raise the arms overhead, palms facing each other.
Exhale and bend the front knee toward a right angle, knee over the ankle; the back leg stays straight and strong.
Lift the chest, relax the shoulders away from the ears and gaze ahead.
Hold 15 seconds to a minute; straighten the front leg, lower the arms and repeat on the other side.
warrior1.works: Strengthens the legs and back, stretches the hip flexors, arms and shoulders, expands the chest and lungs; builds stamina and confidence.
warrior1.watch: The front knee falling inward or past the ankle, the back heel lifting, the lower back over-arching, hips turned to the side.
warrior1.easier: Shorter stance, front knee only slightly bent, back foot turned out more; hands on the hips.
warrior1.tip: If the lower back feels pinched, lean the torso a little forward over the front thigh and draw the tailbone down.
warrior1.avoid: High blood pressure or a heart condition — keep the hands on the hips. Knee, hip or shoulder injury. During menstruation.

steps: Lie on the back, knees bent, feet hip-width apart close to the buttocks.
Place the palms beside the ears, fingers pointing toward the shoulders.
Exhale and lift the pelvis; then come onto the crown of the head.
Exhale again and straighten the arms, lifting the head off the floor and arching the whole back.
Stretch the legs and arms, keeping the feet and hands parallel; hold a few breaths.
Bend the elbows and knees and lower slowly, head first; hug the knees to the chest.
wheel.works: A full backbend that tones the spine, strengthens the arms, wrists, legs and abdomen, opens the chest and gives energy and lightness.
wheel.watch: Feet and knees splaying out, pushing from the lower back only, collapsing onto the head.
wheel.easier: Stay in bridge; or practise over a chair or bolster with a teacher.
wheel.tip: Work on opening the shoulders and the fronts of the thighs first — that is what makes the arch even.
wheel.avoid: Back, wrist or shoulder problems, high or low blood pressure, heart conditions, headache, pregnancy.

steps: Step the feet about a leg-length apart, parallel, toes forward; hands on the hips.
Inhale and lift the chest; exhale and fold forward from the hips with a flat back.
Place the palms on the floor shoulder-width apart, under the shoulders.
Lengthen the spine: crown of the head toward the floor, sitting bones up.
Bend the elbows and bring the head toward the floor between the hands; relax the neck.
Hold 30 seconds to a minute; hands back to the hips, come up with a flat back on an inhale.
wide.works: Stretches the inner legs and back; head below the heart calms.
wide.watch: Feet turned out and weight on the heels.
wide.easier: Hands on blocks or a chair, back flat.
wide.tip: Rest the crown of the head on a block or bolster: this turns the pose into a calming rest at the end of the standing poses.
wide.avoid: Lower back injury; uncontrolled high blood pressure.

steps: Stand with the feet about a leg-length apart, parallel, toes forward.
Exhale and fold forward with a flat back; palms on the floor under the shoulders.
Move the left hand to the centre, under the face, and press it down.
Inhale and raise the right arm to the ceiling, turning the chest to the right.
Look up at the hand, or at the floor if the neck is tight; hold 15–30 seconds.
Lower the arm and repeat to the other side; bring the feet closer and roll up slowly.
widetwist.works: Stretches the hamstrings and inner thighs while twisting the spine; tones the abdomen, releases the upper back and opens the chest.
widetwist.watch: Twisting from the neck rather than the ribs, the hips shifting sideways, the back rounding.
widetwist.easier: The bottom hand on a block; bend the knees slightly.
widetwist.tip: Breathe evenly and go a little deeper into the twist with each exhale; come up very slowly to avoid dizziness.
widetwist.avoid: High blood pressure, headache, lower back problems; skip if it makes you dizzy.

steps: Kneel and sit back on the heels, knees hip-width apart (or sit in lotus).
Interlace the fingers behind the back and press the hands down to lengthen the arms.
Inhale and open the chest, drawing the shoulder blades together.
Exhale and fold forward from the hips toward the floor.
Raise the clasped arms behind you as far as is comfortable, forehead toward the floor.
Hold 30 seconds to a minute; come up with a flat back on an inhale.
yogamudra.works: Stretches the shoulders, upper back and neck, helps correct rounded shoulders, stimulates the abdomen and digestion; quietens the mind.
yogamudra.watch: The buttocks lifting high off the heels, forcing the arms, the neck straining.
yogamudra.easier: Hold a strap between the hands; a folded blanket between the heels and buttocks or under the forehead.
yogamudra.tip: In lotus, the heels press into the belly as you fold — this gently massages the colon and helps sluggish digestion.
yogamudra.avoid: Neck, shoulder, arm or knee problems; high blood pressure.
